capabilities.target: HR policy search index (published policies only)

inputs.source: HR policy search index content (HR-maintained, published policies, write restricted with two-person review)

instructions.note: "Do not give legal advice" is enforced only by model compliance (behavioral, dependent). No structural guardrail (e.g., output filter) backs this instruction. Low severity because the agent's capability surface is read-only and egress is bound to the asking employee, limiting the harm of a lapse.

elements.name: HR content team two-person publishing review

controls.name: Read-only, least-privilege credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by credential issuance outside the model; a more capable model cannot use access the credential does not grant. Only fails if the scope itself widens (data_scope_expansion) or the credential is reissued more broadly (control_removal).

controls.name: No tools beyond policy_search, no memory, no network egress (network-layer deny, pen-test verified)
controls.decay_rationale: Egress is denied at the network layer, independent of model behavior, and verified by a pen test. The agent has no capability to reach any destination other than the one declared tool and the chat reply channel, so no model behavior can open a side-channel today. Fails only if a new tool or network path is added (new_tool, new_mcp_server) or the rule is removed (control_removal).

controls.name: Reply destination bound to the authenticated session; chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: The reply destination comes from the authenticated session record, not from model output, so the model cannot redirect disclosure to another recipient. The no-render restriction closes the classic image/link side-channel exfiltration vector regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Write access to the policy index restricted to the HR content team; publishing requires two-person review
controls.decay_rationale: Write access is enforced by organizational access control and a dual-review publishing process outside the agent and outside the model. The agent itself holds no write capability to this store (see ctl.credential_scope), so neither the model nor an external untrusted party can poison the index through the agent.

controls.name: Model version pinned; upgrade requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: The pin is a change-management gate enforced outside the model; it does not itself decay with capability, but it only slows the model_upgrade trigger rather than preventing it, since a ticket can approve an upgrade without necessarily re-running this assessment.

controls.name: System prompt restricts the agent to published HR policy Q&A and forbids legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to follow the instruction. A more capable or adversarially prompted model could frame legal interpretation as policy explanation, or quietly expand scope beyond published policy.

controls.name: Audit logging of tool calls and replies
controls.decay_rationale: Would not decay with model capability since enforcement sits in logging infrastructure, not the model. Not declared in the provided artifacts.

controls.name: Per-user rate limit on policy_search calls
controls.decay_rationale: Not declared; would bound query volume and downstream cost independent of model behavior.

findings.title: Published HR policy content reaches the employee through the chat reply channel (I source to S2 sink)

attack_path.note: Authenticated employee asks a question, triggering a search.
Returns retrieved internal content as egress (is_egress true, data_sensitivity internal) into the bound session.
Destination is fixed to the authenticated requester's own session.

evidence.observation: Policy index holds only published policies; data sensitivity internal; write restricted to the HR content team with two-person review before publishing.
Agent credential is read-only and scoped to the policy index (least privilege), narrowing cap.policy_search.
Replies go only to the authenticated requester's own chat session; the client does not render images or auto-fetch links, closing side-channel egress routes.
System prompt scopes the agent to quoting published policy, directs it to say when a policy does not answer the question, and forbids legal advice; this is a behavioral, dependent control only.

recommendations.action: Add audit logging of tool invocations and replies, tied to the authenticated session id, to support repudiation resistance and future reassessment evidence.
Add a per-user rate limit on policy_search calls to bound volume independent of model behavior.

findings.title: If tooling or data scope expands, the current egress containment and credential scoping fail to generalize (TC1-adjacent shape)

attack_path.note: If data_scope_expansion widens the index to confidential or restricted HR content (e.g., individual case records), this read carries higher sensitivity.
Scope boundary that would widen under data_scope_expansion.
The existing egress channel would now carry confidential data; a new_tool/new_mcp_server addition could also open exposure not covered by the current pen-tested network denial.

evidence.observation: Only one tool (policy_search.search) is declared today; no other tools, memory, or egress exist, so this finding is conditional on a future change, not a path that exists now.

The scoped credential and the single-tool, no-egress boundary are the only structural controls preventing a wider reach; both are classified independent/partially_dependent only within the current scope and tool set.

forecast.watch_signal: A diff on tools.json or an MCP client config adding any entry beyond policy_search.search; or documentation/index-schema changes indicating non-published or confidential HR content categories (e.g., individual case data) added to the search scope.

recommendations.action: Require this assessment to be rerun, and the credential scope and network-egress denial to be re-verified, before any new tool, MCP server, or data category is added to this agent.

rating.rationale: Only one present-horizon path exists: internal, write-restricted HR policy content reaches the asking employee through the chat reply channel (an internal-trust source feeding an S2 egress sink, since is_egress is true and data_sensitivity is internal). Inherent is moderate (I to S2 per the base matrix); no autonomy modifier applies because autonomy is A3 with small, bounded step/runtime limits and no spawning or self-configuration. Credential scoping to read-only/least-privilege (rubric step 3, structural/independent, -1 tier) and the prompt's scope and no-legal-advice instruction (step 4, behavioral/dependent, -1 tier) bring residual to the rubric floor of low. Recipient binding, the no-image/no-autolink chat client, the pen-test-verified network egress denial, and the two-person review gate on policy publishing further sever adjacent sub-paths (reply misdirection, hidden side-channel egress, index poisoning) even though they are not needed to reach the floor on this finding. No lethal-trifecta or other toxic combination pattern applies today because there is no untrusted (U) source anywhere in the design and no write, execute, spend, or configure capability exists at all. Forecast rises to high: the single-tool allowlist and the network egress denial are structural but scope-bound (partially_dependent in practice), and the scoped credential is independent only until the scope itself changes. A new_tool, new_mcp_server, or data_scope_expansion trigger -- for example widening the policy index to confidential HR case data, or adding a tool with its own egress -- would reclassify the sink to S3 and remove the containment these controls currently provide, per control_decay.md. The single highest-leverage item to watch is ctl.no_other_egress: it is the control whose failure under an additive trigger does the most to move the forecast.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, tools.json, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP config, IaC, or credential policy file was provided. The read-only, policy-index-scoped credential is taken as declared; only the network-layer egress denial is described as pen-test verified. Confidence on the credential scoping claim is accordingly medium rather than high.

max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not stated in the artifacts; low values were inferred from the single-tool, single-turn design described. If the actual deployment allows looping or batched queries, the autonomy modifier in rubric section 4 should be revisited.
No logging or observability artifact was provided, so the missing audit-log control (ctl.missing_audit_log) could not be confirmed as absent versus simply undocumented.
